draft.title: Nature and nurture together
card: the genes a person inherits from their biological parents. Genes shape traits such as height, and can make some abilities or conditions more likely.
everything a person experiences after conception, such as family, friends, school, food and culture.
Development comes from heredity and environment working together. Neither one acts alone.
Genes can set a range, and the environment influences where a person ends up in it. A child with genes for tallness may not reach their height if they lack enough food.
draft.remember: Genes and environment work together, so neither explains development alone.

a.q: Which statement best describes how development occurs?
opts: Genes and environment influence each other's effects
Genes decide development and environment adds little
Environment decides development and genes add little
Genes act first, then environment takes over fully
a.why: Development comes from heredity and environment working together, so each shapes how the other has its effect. The options that name only one cause ignore the other, and the last wrongly splits them into separate stages.
a.clue: Think about whether either factor works on its own.

b.q: Two children in Ballarat inherit genes linked to strong musical ability. Only Lena has music lessons and a family that encourages practice. Lena becomes a skilled musician and her sibling Tom does not. What does this best show?
opts: Inherited ability needs a supportive environment to develop
Genes had no effect on how Lena developed
Lessons alone explain why Lena became skilled
Tom's genes were weaker than Lena's genes
b.why: Both children share the genes, but only Lena had an environment that helped the ability grow. This shows heredity and environment working together. Saying lessons alone explain it is tempting, but it ignores the genes that made the ability possible.
b.clue: Both children have the same genes, so what differs?

a.best: Genes and environment influence each other's effects

b.best: Inherited ability needs a supportive environment to develop

problems.detail: The clue says 'Both children have the same genes', but Lena and Tom are siblings, not stated to be identical twins. Siblings share only about half their genes. The stem only says both inherited genes linked to musical ability, so the clue teaches something false about heredity.
The stem opens with 'Two children' and then calls Tom 'her sibling', which reads as if a relationship is being added late. It is slightly confusing.

The right option is clearly the longest (about 59 characters against about 41 to 44 for the others) and the only general, principle-style statement, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

The right option says inherited ability 'needs' a supportive environment, but the card says only that the environment influences where a person ends up in the range and that a child 'may not' reach their potential. 'Needs' overstates the card.
